sections.h2: Where is Wayne County, Ohio, and what surrounds its tax offices?
sections.html:
Wayne County sits in the northeastern quarter of Ohio, with Wooster as both county seat and largest city. The county was described in legislation in 1808 and formally organized in January 1812, and it carries the name of General Anthony Wayne. It touches Medina and Summit counties on the north, Stark on the east, Holmes on the south and Ashland on the west.

The land area is about 555 square miles, and the Wooster micropolitan area is defined by this one county. High schools in the county include Wooster, Orrville, Rittman, Smithville, Dalton, Chippewa, Northwestern, Norwayne, Triway and Waynedale, and the College of Wooster is based in the county seat. The Auditor, Treasurer and Recorder all work from the Administration Building at 428 West Liberty Street in Wooster, so a seller can visit all three on one trip.

sections.h2: What do Census figures say about Wayne County homeowners?
sections.html:
Wayne County is a place where most people own the house they live in. The Census Bureau's QuickFacts page lists 116,758 residents for July 2025, 44,365 households, and an owner-occupied rate of 76.6 percent for 2020 to 2024.

  • Median value of an owner-occupied home: $222,100.
  • Median monthly owner cost with a mortgage: $1,440. Without a mortgage: $561.
  • Median gross rent: $881.
  • Median household income: $73,574 (2024 dollars).
  • Building permits issued in 2025: 232.

The Auditor's own home page lists a parcel count of 59,000 and an area of 554.8 square miles, which gives a sense of how many bills the Treasurer mails twice a year.

sections.h2: How is a Wayne County real estate tax bill built?
sections.html:
The Auditor's office explains that each parcel is taxed on 35 percent of its market value, and that 35 percent figure is the assessed or taxable value. That number is multiplied by the rate for your tax district, then trimmed by a reduction factor so voted levies do not collect more than voters approved.

  • Most residential parcels also get the non-business credit that dates to 1971.
  • An owner-occupied home can get a further credit on the dwelling and up to one acre of home site.
  • County millage funds the general fund, children services, the County Care Center, Medway Drug Enforcement and the board of developmental disabilities.
  • Townships, municipalities and school districts add their own levies. Libraries, fire districts and Wayne Holmes Mental Health appear under "Other" on the bill's distribution panel.

Ohio caps unvoted millage at 10 mills, and the Treasurer's site posts a chart of tax districts and rates so you can see which one applies to your street.

sections.h2: When are Wayne County property taxes due, and what does a late payment cost?
sections.html:
Taxes come due twice a year, in February and July, and the exact dates are printed on each bill. First half bills go out in January or February, and second half bills in June or July. For 2026 the Treasurer posted the dates in the table below.

2026 collection dates posted on the Wayne County Treasurer's website
InstallmentDue for banksDue to the Treasurer
First halfFebruary 2, 2026February 26, 2026
Second halfJuly 13, 2026July 30, 2026

The Treasurer's FAQ says a 10 percent penalty attaches after the due date, and the county auditor remits half of it if the full amount arrives within 10 days. Credit and debit payments carry a processor fee of 2.35 percent with a $2.00 minimum, and an e-check costs $0.50. A returned check adds $15.00. Mailed payments rely on the postmark, but the Treasurer warns that postmarks can lag the drop-off date, and it does not honor postmarks during the September delinquent cycle.

If no bill has arrived by July 1, call the Treasurer at 330-287-5450. Ohio law (R.C. 323.13) says a bill that never reached you does not excuse the payment.

sections.h2: How does a Wayne County owner challenge a valuation?
sections.html:
The route runs through the Wayne County Board of Revision. A complaint is filed between January 1 and March 31, and under R.C. 5715.19 the deadline can stretch to the close of first half collection when that falls later. The Auditor's page for the 2026 tax year gives January 1, 2027 through March 31, 2027 as the window.

  • The complaint must be signed and notarized. Auditor staff can usually notarize forms brought in person.
  • A mailed complaint needs a postmark by March 31. Email and fax filings must arrive by 11:59 pm that day.
  • Only one complaint is allowed per triennial cycle, unless the property sold at arm's length, suffered a casualty loss, gained a substantial improvement, or saw a 15 percent shift in occupancy.
  • Pay the first half bill. The second half bill is held until the complaint is decided, and any over or underpayment is settled on it.

The county's 2026 reappraisal has its own timeline. The Auditor's home page says the informal appeal deadline for that reappraisal has passed and that Board of Revision filings open January 1, 2027. The Board of Revision phone line is 330-287-5433.

sections.h2: Which Wayne County tax reduction programs can a homeowner use?
sections.html:
The Auditor administers the homestead exemption, the owner-occupied credit and the current agricultural use value program. Forms are posted on the Auditor's site, including the DTE 105A homestead application, DTE 105B continuing application, DTE 105C owner-occupancy application, DTE 105E disability certificate and DTE 105I for disabled veterans and surviving spouses.

Wayne County also lists tax exemption applications for churches, schools, nonprofits and public land. Income limits and age rules change from year to year, so ask the Auditor's real estate division at 330-287-5430 which limits apply to the current tax year before you rely on a credit in a sale.

sections.h2: What do sellers pay at the Auditor and Recorder in Wayne County?
sections.html:
A deed in Wayne County goes through three desks in the same building. It first visits the Map Office, next the Auditor, then the Recorder. At the Auditor's counter the posted conveyance fee is $4.00 per thousand of the sale price plus a $0.50 transfer fee per parcel, and the office rounds the price up to the next $100.

  • Recording fees printed on the Auditor's page: $34.00 for the first two pages and $8.00 for each added page.
  • Marginal notations cost $4.00, copies $2.00, and a standardization guideline fee is $20.00.
  • Before the Auditor endorses a deed, the buyer files a statement of value under R.C. 319.202, which also asks about agricultural use recoupment.
  • The Auditor's Conveyance Fee Calculator, Tax Estimator and Levy Estimator are online tools for a first look at the numbers.

Property tax prorations are handled between buyer and seller in the purchase contract, so ask the Treasurer for a payoff figure on any parcel with a balance. The delinquent list on the Treasurer's site shows whether a parcel has unpaid years.

faqs.q: When are Wayne County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Twice a year, in February and July. The Treasurer's 2026 dates were February 26 for the first half and July 30 for the second, with earlier bank dates of February 2 and July 13. Each bill prints its own due date.

faqs.q: What is the Wayne County Board of Revision filing window?
faqs.a: January 1 through March 31, with the Auditor listing January 1, 2027 to March 31, 2027 for tax year 2026. The complaint must be notarized, and mail needs a March 31 postmark.

faqs.q: How much is the Wayne County conveyance fee?
faqs.a: The Auditor's page prints $4.00 per thousand of the sale price plus $0.50 per parcel, rounded up to the next $100. Use the Auditor's Conveyance Fee Calculator to see your own figure.

faqs.q: Can I pay a Wayne County tax bill by card?
faqs.a: Yes. The Treasurer accepts cards, Apple Pay, Google Pay and Samsung Pay online, by phone at 1-844-615-1900, or in person. The processor fee is 2.35 percent with a $2.00 minimum, and e-check costs $0.50.

faqs.q: Where do I record the deed after a Wayne County sale?
faqs.a: At the Recorder's Office, 428 West Liberty Street in Wooster, first floor, phone 330-287-5460, after the Auditor endorses it. The Recorder keeps deeds, mortgages, liens and subdivision plats.
